multiOmicsSuite

Source: AGENTS.md

Description

multiOmicsSuite (MOSuite) is an R package for differential multi-omic analysis. It defines an S7 class called multiOmicDataSet to store data and analyses from multi-omic experiments.

Development of MOSuite follows the R packages 2nd edition (https://r-pkgs.org/), with a few minor exceptions noted below. Helper functions from usethis and devtools are used extensively for development tasks. Human developers should refer to the contributing guidelines for detailed instructions on how to contribute to MOSuite.

Package conventions

  • Internal functions should have roxygen2 documentation (with @keywords internal). Do not strip roxygen docs from internal functions.
  • R code should pass lintr and air format (run air format . from the package root).
  • Tests should be written with testthat.
  • The package must pass devtools::check().
  • R code should adhere to the tidyverse style guide. https://style.tidyverse.org/
  • Only include one return statement at the end of a function. Explicit returns are preferred but not required for R functions.
  • NAMESPACE and man/ are generated by devtools::document() and in the auto-format workflow; never edit these files directly.

Commit messages

  • Check for user approval before running commit commands. The git commit command should be shown expanded (with the full -m message text visible), not collapsed or abbreviated, so the user can see the exact message before it runs.
  • If approval has not been given, proceed with code changes and tests only; do not commit.
  • Commit messages must follow Conventional Commits (as enforced in CONTRIBUTING.md).
  • Generate messages from staged changes only (git diff --staged); do not include unrelated work.
  • Commits should be atomic: one logical change per commit.
  • If mixed changes are present, split into multiple logical commits; the number of commits does not need to equal the number of files changed.
  • Before staging, review git status and git diff to confirm the change set is small enough to describe in one sentence; if not, it likely needs to be split.
  • Do not blanket-stage with git add . or git add -A; stage files or hunks individually (git add <file>, git add -p) so unrelated changes are not swept into the same commit.
  • When splitting into multiple commits, order them so each commit leaves the repository in a working state (e.g., dependencies/config before the code that uses them).
  • Do not mix mechanical changes (formatting, renames, regenerated files) with substantive logic changes in the same commit.
  • Subject format must be: <type>(optional-scope): short imperative summary (<=72 chars), e.g., fix(profile): update release table parser.
  • Add a body only when needed to explain why and notable impact; never include secrets, tokens, PHI, or large diffs.
  • For commits containing any AI-generated code, commit messages, or any other AI-generated content, add this final italicized footer line in the commit message body: “AI assistance: [model]”. Replace [model] with the actual model version used, e.g. Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, etc.

Pull request (PR) process

  • PR titles must follow Conventional Commits format (see “Commit messages” section).
  • When opening a PR, use the request template (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) and fill out all sections of the template in the PR description. Do not allow the developer to proceed with opening a PR if the PR does not fill out all sections of the template.
  • Go through the PR template section-by-section in order:
    1. Changes: Summarize user-facing behavior changes, bug fixes, or design decisions.
    2. Issues: Reference any related issues using keywords.
    3. Generative AI Usage Statement: Determine if AI was used for any part of this PR. If yes, uncomment this section and fill it in. If no, leave commented or uncomment and state “No generative AI tools were used”.
    4. PR Checklist: Process items sequentially (see checklist workflow below).
  • Write drafted PR descriptions to a gitignored file at .github/PR_DRAFT.md (overwrite if it already exists). Tell the developer where the file is and instruct them to review and edit it before using it — do not treat a draft as final or ready to ship without that review.
  • When drafting a PR description, initialize every checklist item in .github/PR_DRAFT.md with one explicit state:
    • use - [x] when the item is verified by evidence (agent-run command output or explicit developer confirmation),
    • use - [ ] when the item is relevant and pending verification,
    • use - ~[ ] item text~ when the item is not applicable.
  • Before processing checklist items, examine the current branch state with git status and git diff to understand what has already been modified. Do not add NEWS.md entries or other changes that may already be in the branch.
  • Quick open: use Cmd+Click on .github/PR_DRAFT.md in the editor.
  • Before asking for permission to run gh pr create, explicitly prompt the developer to open .github/PR_DRAFT.md, review/edit it, and confirm that review is complete.
  • Apply this formatting consistently for both initial draft creation and all later checklist edits.
  • Process checklist items sequentially, one item at a time, before opening the PR.
  • For each checklist item:
    • collect evidence,
    • document evidence in the Changes section if it supports a feature or fix (e.g., “Added examples using synthetic data”),
    • update only the checklist state (checked, unchecked, or crossed out) in .github/PR_DRAFT.md immediately — do not append evidence descriptions to checklist items.
  • If evidence cannot be collected automatically, ask the developer for confirmation, record that confirmation in the PR draft, and then update the checklist state.
  • Agents may open a PR with relevant pending items left as - [ ] only if the PR is opened as a draft.
  • Agents must not open a non-draft (ready-for-review) PR while any relevant checklist item remains pending (- [ ]).
  • Whenever an AI agent assists with creating or drafting a PR (including this exact workflow — a developer asking the agent to open or draft a PR), the PR is considered to have generative AI-assisted content and must be labeled AI-assisted.
  • The “Generative AI Usage Statement” heading in the PR template (which is commented out by default) must be uncommented and filled in with a brief, concise statement of how generative AI was used (model used, high-level prompt intent, manual review confirmation, etc.), regardless of whether the underlying code/commits were themselves generated by generative AI.
  • To open the PR, either:
    • Instruct the user to paste the reviewed contents of .github/PR_DRAFT.md into GitHub’s web UI, or
    • run gh pr create --title "<conventional-commit-style title>" --body-file .github/PR_DRAFT.md (add --draft if the PR should open as a draft, and --label "AI-assisted" if applicable). Only run gh pr create with explicit developer approval, and only after prompting the developer to open .github/PR_DRAFT.md and receiving confirmation that review/edit is complete. Point the user to .github/PR_DRAFT.md for final review.
    • If the AI-assisted label was not added at creation time, add it afterwards with gh pr edit <PR-number-or-URL> --add-label "AI-assisted".
  • When new features, bug fixes, or other behavioral changes are introduced to the code, unit tests must be added or updated to cover the new or changed functionality; unit tests should not be skipped without a strong reason.
  • If there are any API or other user-facing changes, the documentation must be updated both inline via roxygen comments and long-form docs in the vignettes/ directory as R Markdown files.
  • Before a PR can be moved from draft to “ready for review”, all of the relevant checklist items must be checked, and any irrelevant checklist items should be crossed out.
  • If there are merge conflicts, a human developer must resolve them. AI agents must not agree to assist with resolving merge conflicts. Human developers who are unsure how to proceed should reach out to the lead maintainer or code owner.
  • The R-CMD-check github actions workflow must pass before the PR can be approved.

Changelog

The changelog for the repository is maintained in NEWS.md at the root of the repository. Each pull request that introduces user-facing changes must include a concise entry with the PR number (not the issue number) and author’s github username tagged. Developer-only changes (i.e. updates to CI workflows, development notes, internal developer documentation like AGENTS.md or PR templates, etc.) should never be included in the changelog.

Example:

## development version

- Fix bug in `detect_absolute_paths()` to ignore comments. (#123, @github-username)
